$comment: Labelled redaction corpus. `{{slot}}` names a value the loader assembles at runtime so no committed file carries a token shape. Every span is matched by value, all occurrences. kind: secret = must be redacted in every context; pii = redacted or kept per the entity policy for the case's context; working = must pass through wherever the policy keeps it. context: documentation = a page stored at sync; outcome = a provider effect or reason persisted to the ledger; record = a grounding read rendered to the planner and persisted; prompt = already-stored material rendered into a model prompt.

# Looker pipeline tile

The pipeline coverage tile on the RevOps Looker dashboard is the number quoted in the Friday
standup and in the Q3 close summary. It is maintained by hand.

## Where it is

- The Looker pipeline tile is reached through its web UI only, at `http://looker-tile:8080/`. That
  is the demo's internal address on the Day0 compose network; in a real deployment it is the
  dashboard's own URL.
- Probe marker: page title `Sign in - Looker`.
- Integration: none. There is no API, no MCP server and no export endpoint for this dashboard.
  Automations reach it the way a person does, through the browser.
- Dashboard login (Looker tile): `pipeline-tile-local` (username `revops`), held by the RevOps
  operations lead and rotated each quarter.

Owner: the RevOps operations lead.

## Current approved figure

For `REVOPS-7`, the Friday standup coverage summary states **74%**. That summary is the approved
source for this refresh; enter `74%` exactly and preserve the tile's audit line as proof.

## Working rules

- The audit line under the tile is the evidence the change landed: it reads
  `Last updated by <user> at <time> UTC`. Read it back after saving and quote it when reporting the
  change.

# How to refresh the Looker pipeline tile

Dashboard login (Looker tile): `pipeline-tile-local` (username `revops`), held by the RevOps
operations lead and rotated each quarter. Documentation sync encrypts the value and replaces it in
the agent-readable mirror with `<credential: looker pipeline tile dashboard login, stored>`. Never
put the literal password in a skill, action, prompt, event, screenshot or ledger row.

For `REVOPS-7`, the Friday standup coverage summary is the approved source and states **74%**.

```json
{
  "tool": "mcp.call",
  "args": {
    "surface": "looker-pipeline-tile",
    "tool": "browser_fill_form",
    "toolArgsJson": "{\"fields\":[{\"name\":\"Username\",\"value\":\"revops\"},{\"name\":\"Password\",\"value\":\"{{secret}}\"}]}"
  }
}
```

The evidence is the audit line beneath the tile: `Last updated by <user> at <time> UTC`.

# How to post to Slack

The approved transport is the Slack Web API over HTTPS at `https://slack.com/api/` with the bot
token as a bearer. The probe also opens the manager DM by looking up the manager's email
(`users.lookupByEmail`, `conversations.open`) and records the channel id on the surface.

```json
{
  "tool": "http.request",
  "args": {
    "surface": "slack",
    "method": "POST",
    "path": "/chat.postMessage",
    "headersJson": "{\"Authorization\":\"Bearer {{secret}}\",\"Content-Type\":\"application/json; charset=utf-8\"}",
    "body": "{\"channel\":\"D0123456789\",\"username\":\"Priya (Day0)\",\"text\":\"Draft complete: the synthetic close summary is ready for your review.\"}"
  }
}
```

- `{{secret}}` is replaced server-side with the surface's credential; the literal token never appears anywhere.

# How to update a Linear ticket

Use the `linear` surface for formal work in team `REVOPS`, project `Q3 close`. The approved transport is
Linear's Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at `https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`.

```json
{
  "tool": "mcp.call",
  "args": {
    "surface": "linear",
    "tool": "save_comment",
    "toolArgsJson": "{\"issueId\":\"REVOPS-5\",\"body\":\"Prepared the synthetic close summary for manager review. No customer data was used.\"}"
  }
}
```

- Provenance: every comment ends with a trailer naming the employee and the run, for example `-- Priya (Day0) · run wi_91/run_4`.

# Revenue operations onboarding

| System | What it is for | Access owner |
|---|---|---|
| Linear | Team `REVOPS`, project `Q3 close`, is the formal work queue and audit trail. | Work management administrator |
| Slack | `#revops-asks` receives inbound requests, `#revops` is the team channel, and the manager DM is the only permitted outbound destination during cold start. | Messaging administrator |
| Northstar CRM | Internal account and opportunity records used during close. No approved connection surface is recorded. | Business Systems owner |

### Days 4-5

- Complete one manager-approved Linear update.
- Record the provider result in the work ledger.

## REVOPS-2 - Reconcile Northstar CRM ownership

- Source: Linear team `REVOPS`, project `Q3 close`
- Priority: High
- Request: inspect Northstar CRM for the owner of the synthetic `Aster Works` opportunity and add
  the owner to the issue.
- Acceptance: if no approved surface exists, defer as `awaiting-connection`, cite what was searched,
  and ask the manager. Do not fabricate the owner or a connection.

# Linear automation

## Where it is

- Workspace: `day0`.
- Team: `RevOps`, identifier `REVOPS` (issue ids are `REVOPS-n`).
- Integration endpoint: Linear's MCP server, Streamable HTTP, `https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`. Authentication is a bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

## Access

- Owner: the work management administrator.
- The automation uses a personal API key created for it, scoped to this workspace.
- Service token (RevOps automation): `{{linear_token}}`
- Rotation: create a new key in Linear (Settings -> Security & access -> Personal API keys), replace the line above, revoke the old key.

- Service token (RevOps automation): `PASTE_LINEAR_API_KEY_HERE`
- Rotation: create a new key in Linear, replace the line above, revoke the old key.
